comparator.name: Information Science
comparator.sourceNotes: Open Universiteit offers this Dutch-taught degree part-time. It comprises 55 EC of compulsory foundation courses, 65 EC of later taught courses, 15 EC of restricted electives, 30 EC of free electives and a 15 EC graduation project.
components: Choose three courses from the six approved analytics and innovation electives.
Complete 60 EC of foundation study, including the required academic skills course.
Choose eligible courses. The suggested study schedules include 5 EC of electives alongside the compulsory foundation courses.
Complete Graduation Project Preparation immediately before starting the project.

core: Information systems, programming, databases, modelling and user requirements
Organisations, business operations and IT project implementation
Data, analytics, statistics and information-science research
Privacy, information security, ethical innovation and societal effects
adjacent: Computational data science and mathematical modelling
Programming, software design and technical systems development
questions: How can information systems connect organisational needs, data and users?
How can organisations analyse data and adopt digital technology responsibly?

alternatives.label: Information Systems and Digital Organizations
alternatives.concept: Study how organizations design, adopt and evaluate digital systems. Combine programming, databases and data analysis with business, accounting, product design, user research and responsible technology.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how organizations design, adopt and evaluate digital systems. Combine programming, databases and data analysis with business, accounting, product design, user research and responsible technology.
progression: Programming and research foundations precede data and user inquiry. Business foundations and product design precede digital strategy and advanced organizational study.

alternatives.label: Data Science and Information Analysis
alternatives.concept: Use programming, statistics and mathematical models to make sense of data. Study databases, data preparation, research design, machine learning and models of dynamic systems, then apply these tools to questions about organizations and their users.
alternatives.labelReason: Use programming, statistics and mathematical models to make sense of data. Study databases, data preparation, research design, machine learning and models of dynamic systems, then apply these tools to questions about organizations and their users.
progression: Programming, introductory data study and linear algebra precede modeling and machine learning. Data methods and machine learning precede deep learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Use programming, statistics and mathematical models to make sense of data. Study databases, data preparation, research design, machine learning and models of dynamic systems, then apply these tools to questions about organizations and their users. Each plan has 5 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.

alternatives.label: Software, Computer Systems and Algorithms
alternatives.concept: Learn to develop software and design algorithms, then study databases, networks and operating systems. Mathematical methods and AI extend the technical foundation. This plan emphasizes the computing side of information science.
alternatives.labelReason: Learn to develop software and design algorithms, then study databases, networks and operating systems. Mathematical methods and AI extend the technical foundation. This plan emphasizes the computing side of information science.
progression: Programming and discrete mathematics precede algorithms and advanced software. Linear algebra and introductory data study precede later quantitative and AI work.
alternatives.distinctness: Learn to develop software and design algorithms, then study databases, networks and operating systems. Mathematical methods and AI extend the technical foundation. This plan emphasizes the computing side of information science. Each plan has 10 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 8 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.

candidates.label: Data and information management with analytics

selection.assessment: The closest plan combines information technology, organizations, accounting and research. The analytics plan emphasizes statistics, quantitative modeling and machine learning. The technical plan emphasizes software, networks and advanced algorithms. Privacy and responsible deployment receive substantive treatment across the plans, while dedicated information security, enterprise modeling, ontology and specialist project preparation remain gaps.

blocks: Both introduce computing. UCR concentrates on programming and computational problem solving.
Both study logic, sets, relations and formal reasoning.
Both develop object-oriented programming. UCR also introduces functional programming.
Open Universiteit requires dedicated software engineering. UCR teaches related development practices in a broader course.
Open Universiteit teaches enterprise modeling as a dedicated subject.
The UCR plans explore information science through courses in computing, data and organizations.
Both study relational database design and SQL.
Both develop communication for different audiences. Open Universiteit includes professional practice.
Open Universiteit teaches information security as a dedicated subject. UCR covers privacy and accountability in Ethics of AI.
Open Universiteit teaches object-oriented analysis and design. UCR’s product course addresses user needs and prototyping.
Open Universiteit offers dedicated study of representing domain knowledge.
Both use data analysis to inform decisions. UCR develops general data analysis techniques.
Both develop statistical inference. UCR also provides a mathematical treatment of probability.
Both develop research design and evidence analysis. Open Universiteit requires 60 EC of foundation study, including the academic skills course, before its 10 EC methods course.
Both examine how AI affects people and organizations. UCR emphasizes business and economic effects.
Both study behavior, motivation and teams in organizations.
Both address budgeting, costing and performance. UCR also covers financial accounting and investment appraisal.
Both examine how organizations operate. UCR approaches this through business foundations.
Open Universiteit requires a course on setting up and managing projects.
Both develop ethical reasoning. Open Universiteit focuses specifically on digital innovation.
Both examine organizational strategy and technology adoption. UCR focuses on digital transformation.
Academic formation, choice and final research
Both develop academic inquiry and communication.
Complete the rest of the taught program and electives before starting preparation, unless the examiner grants permission.
Choose 30 EC of eligible electives. The suggested study schedules include 5 EC alongside the compulsory foundation courses.
Complete preparation immediately before the supervised 15 EC project. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose three courses from six approved analytics and innovation electives.

notes.text: Both universities offer computing, data analysis and organizational study. Open Universiteit requires dedicated enterprise modeling, ontology, information security and project management, plus information science research methods and a supervised graduation project.

audience.programmeDescription: This Dutch-taught, part-time degree studies how organizations design and use information systems and how digital technology affects people and society.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Open Universiteit combines compulsory courses with analytics and innovation electives and a final research project. The UCR plans emphasize organizational information systems, data analysis, or software and computing.
